Review Title: Do the Glacier Landing, it’s the best part of the tour!
Review Text:
Great experience with K2! This was a once in a lifetime experience for my daughter and I; it was everything we expected and more. The line was long when we arrived but they were fully staffed to meet demand and we were checked in quickly. After checking in we were on the flight within 10 minutes. The pilot was very knowledgeable and easy going. We got some great pictures from the flight and glacier landing.

If you are going to take the tour, I highly recommend the Glacier Landing. It’s more expensive but it really was the highlight of our flight (with the exception of seeing Mt. Denali of course).

Every seat is good in the plane so no need to rush on it to get the best seat. Also we sat in the last two rows since we were the last onboard and we enjoyed have a lot of leg room compared to the other seats.

Some advice for first time flyers specifically re: Glacier Landings:

1. Bring a jacket even if it’s 80 degrees in Talkeetna since the weather changes so much in the mountains. Wear layers if you only have a thin coat. I had a t-shirt and windbreaker but I wish I had something warmer since it was chilly on the glacier during our late evening flight.

2. Wear the boot covers they give you at K2. They keep your shoes dry during the glacier landing!! I was surprised how many folks on our flight did not wear them.

3. Make sure you take lots of photos! Bring an extra camera if you have it. The views are stunning!

I would definitely fly with K2 aviation again!

Review Text:
On two other trips to Alaska I have booked with K2 and had the flights cancelled due to weather. Please note that this was no problem for me. They are not going to fly if it is unsafe or they cannot provide you the experience you are paying for. The money was promptly refunded.

On this trip we arrived in Talkeetna without a tour reservation. As we drove in, I heard the planes taking off from the local airport. I immediately rounded up the family and headed over to see if we could get on a flight. It was no problem and 45 minutes later we were boarding a late afternoon tour.

I believe we were on the Denali Flyer. My sense is the routes are a generalization of length and the areas they will try to show you. I felt like the pilot adjusted the flight based on where things were clear and we could get the best views/experience for the time we had in the air. It is unsafe and pointless to follow a route that is cloud-covered. It was a great tour and I thought the pilot did an excellent job of allowing both sides of the plane to see the different sites. He was informative about the area and things we were seeing. This was the first activity we did in Alaska and set a great tone for the rest of the trip. The family absolutely loved it. We did not have the choice of a glacier landing due to the uncertain weather, so I cannot comment on whether that is a worthwhile addition. I can say that, although expensive, you are not getting the most out of your Alaska trip without some flight seeing. There is just too much of Alaska that is inaccessible from the ground. You need to get into the air to truly get the full experience. Highly recommend K2...take any trip you can afford. If you have the option, I would take a cheaper trip and save money for a second trip of another kind...there is so much to see in this state.

Review Text:
This was a fantastic experience! To see the sheer beauty and majesty of Mt. Denali and Denali National Park from the air is unbelievable. Words and pictures don't do it justice. It was soooo much fun! We had a great time!

Turns out K2 has a generous rescheduling policy. We had scheduled for the "good day" yet Erica called me directly to ask if we could shuffle a bit to help out with guests from the prior day. She gave me a few options and left the decision to alter our plans or not up to me. She and I talked and joked for a while then, in the end, we shifted our reservation by an hour. It was great to meet her in person in Talkeetna. She was super friendly and thanked us again and again for being flexible.
Before boarding the plane, our pilot, Chris, did a great job of putting everyone at ease with a few jokes while explaining how the flight would go and telling us about the plane's safety features. During the flight, he pointed out landmarks, gave us info on the area, and told stories about the mountains. He was very fun and personable and fielded questions from passengers during the flight.
We couldn't be happier with the service from K2. They made the entire experience very, very memorable.

Review Text:
Absolutely one of the top highlights of my recent trip to Alaska. We had signed up for the glacier landing and at check in were told that it was going to be too foggy to land. While we were disappointed and were given the option to reschedule, we didn’t have the schedule flexibility so we agreed to fly without the landing, which we were still very excited about. Once up in the air, our terrific pilot, Chris, had been eying the potential glacier landing field and decided that the conditions were much better than earlier and fog had cleared enough for a safe landing under the premise that we would need to be ready to leave should he sense the conditions changing once on the ground. Standing on the glacier in complete silence listening to rocks falling, glacial water rushing, was one of the most surreal experiences ever. Would 100% recommend this trip and the landing is absolutely worth it. Honorable mention to the way that the bright red plane pops on the white snow in all of our amazing pictures. Thanks, Chris and K2 aviation for the unforgettable experience!

Also, for anyone traveling in the current pandemic climate, K2’s COVID procedures felt very safe and clean and I feel they are doing a great job putting safety first.

Our experience was awesome!

They waterproof shoes that slipped over our own boots for the glacier landing. Our experience was during Covid-19 and the whole staff took extra precautions to ensure our safety and the cleanliness of their airport and planes along with other equipment we came into contact with.

There was some questionable weather in the amphitheater (where they land the plane on the glacier) but our pilot said we would fly in and see how it was when we got there. Luckily, it cleared up and we were able to land. The landing was flawless - which I imagine is not an easy feat on snow and skis. Our pilot took photos of us, taught us so much about glaciers and the surrounding mountains, and was pretty funny as well. He turned the plane a lot to make sure everyone on both sides could see the same things. I have never seen anything more beautiful in my life and I am so happy we sprung for the glacier landing. He also gave us some local tips for places to eat and things to see. I even got to sit copilot on the way back - which was super cool.

On the way back, the landing into Talkeetna airport was just as perfect as the one on the glacier. I was shocked at how smooth both landings were. I would do this again in a heartbeat - it was worth every penny.

Review Text:
My wife and I booked the Denali Experience with Glacier Landing for August 29.

K2 arranged pick-up and drop off service for us at the Talkeetna Lodge. The transfers were completed smoothly. We were informed that since Alaska experienced one of the warmest summers on records the snow on Denali was too soft to conduct the glacier landing. I had been following the latest Tripadvisor reviews and anticipated this situation, disappointing, but totally understandable. Since the tour was prepaid our credit card was reimbursed in a timely manner.

The plane has a capacity of 10 or 11 passengers and we had seven clients on this trip. You are provided with headphones which permit the pilot to narrate information during the flight. The headphones also contained a microphone which allows you to ask questions during the experience.

Each customers has a window seat which provides excellent views and an opportunity for unobstructed photography. Frequently the pilot would maneuver the plane so the passengers on the right side would have a view of a glacier/mountain/point of interest and then adjust the route so the passengers on the left side would have a similar view.

Due to the Swan Lake fire the visibility directly after take-off was less than ideal. The pilot indicated this would clear up as we gained altitude and approached the mountain range. He was 100% correct as visibility was excellent as we approached Denali.

The day before we were fortunate to observe Denali as we exited the park. K2 provided an entirely different visual experience. The excursion is definitely on the expensive side, but since this was likely our one and only trip to Alaska it was totally worth it.

The Denali Experience is the basic of the three tours that K2 offers, for us the length of time in the air was satisfactory.

Our pilot, Chris, was very personable. He came from a family of Alaskan pilots. My wife got to sit in the copilot seat. If they ask who wants to sit there, raise your hand quickly. Flying between peaks was awesome. Landing in the snow in July, wow. It’s pricy...but probably our best experience in our first two weeks in Alaska. And tip your pilot! Don’t be like the majority of passengers on our flight and just shake his hand.

Review Text:
We loved the flightseeing tour of the Alaska Range with a landing on Ruth Glacier. It was an awesome experience!

We made our reservation through Alaska Tour and Travel, just because of some other stuff we were bundling, but you can go straight to the K2 site. They have a nice facility at the airport (soon to be even bigger and nicer with a new facility). Check-in was very organized, and you can enjoy some free coffee while looking at their gift items. They provide overboots for the glacier, so you can just wear your street shoes no problem. We were called by name, introduced to our pilot, and walked to the plane for a quick safety briefing. After takeoff, it is a short flight to get up to the mountains. Our pilot provided interesting information on the area over our headsets. Then you are in the mountains...

We were lucky to have a clear day, and it was specatcular! We flew up the Great Gorge, surrounded by peaks, then by Denali and the other large mountains in the range. Both sides of the airplane get the views. The glacier landing was very cool, and we spent 20 minutes walking around the plane in the huge Sheldon Ampitheater. It is just an incredlble place! The flight back included more awesome views as we zig-zagged down through the peaks (I was sitting up front with the pilot for this part). It was hard to believe we did all this in just 1 1/2 hours.

I highly recommend a flightseeing tour of the Alaska Range and the glacier landing.

Review Text:
I am not a big fan of flying. My fear of heights and motion sickness are the biggest factors. My wife and I were doing a Princess Cruise and she really wanted to see Denali up close and personal. We went out to the airport at Talkeetna and looked at the various different operations offering a flightseeing of Mt. Denali. K2 Aviation seemed to have the best aircraft and most professional facility. We opted for the air tour which included a landing on a glacier near the mountain itself.

We were issued boots and then greeted by our pilot, Stan. Our aircraft was a vintage de Havilland Otter that had been upgraded with modern avionics and a turbine engine. It appeared to be a very well maintained aircraft. After a short safety briefing, we were in the air, heading for the mountain.

There really is no better way to see Denali up close. Weather plays a big factor in determining how close you can get to the mountain and what you can see, but we got lucky with our trip. The views were truly amazing and I managed to get numerous pictures as our pilot wound his way around the numerous mountain peaks. .

Landing on the glacier was fun and the view of the mountain from that location was the best. One minute the peak was covered with clouds and then it was out in the clear.

Soon we were all loaded up and heading off the glacier. After a little more canyon flightseeing, we were on our way back to the airport.

We saw many interesting and wonderful sights on our 12 day Alaska cruise. Without a doubt, the K2 experience was the highlight of the entire trip.

He answered all of our questions and even pointed out base camp so we could get a feel for how high we truly were.  WELL worth it....I can't wait to do it again!

Review Title: Highlight of our week in Alaska
Review Text: At first, a flightseeing trip seemed like a pricey add-on to our Alaska trip, but my son and I were so glad that we decided to go. Our pilot, Chris, was knowledgeable about the geology and history of the mountains in a conversational sort of way, without sounding  like he had memorized a script. Even though the weather didn't allow us to see Denali, it was a spectacular trip that was the highlight of our week in Alaska.

Review Text: Readying to be picked up by the K-2 shuttle at our hotel (Grand Talkeetna Lodge) we were browsing the gift shop when several people mumbled and looked out the rear window to see Denali in all its great splendor. The mountain had been sort of "socked in" for a few days but was now gleaming in the early sunlight of a new day. So with anticipation we boarded the shuttle for the short ride to the K-2 facility, checked in and were assigned to a twin Cessna along with another couple and a family of four with two youngsters. Full cabin but what a great ride! The pilot was most knowledgeable, friendly and put everyone immediately at ease as he "ran up" the engines to check temps and pressures then off we went. The scenery is unimaginable and hard to fully describe in words to convey the full range of the vistas the eye is presented with. Slowly gaining altitude we were soon among the peaks and found ourselves amidst the summit faces of Denali itself. Alas, the experience lasted not long enough as we began our slow descent back down to Talkeetna. As we departed I shook the pilot's hand telling him while I know he had no control over the weather conditions, we were very appreciative of what he was able to show us (and tipped him handsomely for the effort). K-2 is a "cant' miss" deal.

Review Text: Take flight from a small air strip in Talkeetna, AK and soon you'll be looking down at ice fields and glaciers as far as you can see. Cliffs rising thousands of feet in front of you.  Then Denali, the highest mountain on the north American continent looms in front of your small four seater aircraft. The pilot makes a quick turn, dives down, and within a breath or two you're gliding on the snow covered surface of a glacier a mile wide. The plane slows, stops and you step out. Twenty minutes to fill your mind with memories that will last a lifetime before an exciting flight back to Talkeetna. You will never forget this excursion.

Review Text: My son is stationed at JBER and I came to visit for Christmas. He surprised me with this flight tour and I was absolutely amazed at the experience. Review Title: A must do if you're anywhere close to Talkeetna!
Review Text:
We stopped here on our way from Anchorage to Denali...You have to go a bit out of your way to get to Talkeetna, but if you wish to do a flightseeing tour of the Mountain, this is the place

K2 Aviation is the way to go...We had pre-booked (a must) the Summit Tour with a glacier landing, but due to weather conditions were not able to fly to the top of the summit

But, the alternative was amazing...The flight from Talkeetna to the glacier was perfect...Our very knowledgeable pilot provided great information during his commentary...Photo opportunities abounded

The glacier landing is a must add-on (don't worry about the price...this is a once in a lifetime trip)...the scenery is unreal and words won't do it justice...Heck, the photos hardly capture the moment and feeling of wonder

Must do! Must do! Must do!

Review Text:
Wir haben im Juli diese Flightseeing Tour unternommen und konnten auf Grund des nebligen Wetters leider nicht soweit in das vorgesehene Gebiet fliegen wie beabsichtigt.
